content:
Alex: quick heads-up — the hybrid KV pager canary (pager+slab-fallback + kernel-selector tweak) is showing a bad tail regression on paged-attn. noticed ~18% p95 regression vs baseline in canary region. rolling back?
Maria: paste of local bench (short):
```
# bench cmd
./bench --workload paged-attn --seq 2048 --batch 8 --runs 120
# baseline
median=9.7ms p95=33.5ms p99=50.8ms
# canary
median=10.4ms p95=39.6ms p99=64.9ms
# observed logs
kernel_selector: selected=flash_attn_v2 (seq<1024 policy)
kernel_selector: routed_to=fused_attn_v1 (oom-path) xfer
kv_pager: page_faults/sec=+162% vs baseline
alloc: slab_fallback_count=1.2k
```

Raj: interesting — slab_fallback_count up that much suggests fragmentation/reservation mismatch. are we seeing lots of small spills or a few big ones?

Tim: I repro'd and dumped allocator telemetry. summary: many mid-size allocations (~48–256KB) failing fast when contiguous pages not found; pager splits into multiple pages, then slab fallback kicks in which triggers kernel change path (costly).

Jen: perf numbers I have from canary region (prod-like load):
- p50 ~ +8%
- p95 ~ +18%
- p99 ~ +25%
Errors are low but latencies spike during KV warmup windows.

Maria: profiler (cpu wall) shows additional ~6% CPU on pagewalk + 12% on kernel-selection glue code during those spikes. flamegraph from perf-bot below.

perf-bot: flamegraph uploaded: https://ci.internal.redwood/bench/flamegraphs/1718008123/paged-attn-canary (check `pagewalk` and `kernel_dispatch`) :eyes:

ci-bot: ci bench run: https://ci.internal.redwood/bench/runs/1718008123 (includes raw logs + allocator traces)

Raj: proposal: switch allocation strategy for paged-kv to pre-reserve small slab arenas per shard (prefault), reduce need for expensive contiguous pages. also add a fragmentation compaction pass at low-priority GC intervals. avoids heavy slab_fallback churn.

Alex: +1 on trying pre-reserve. can we do a quick AB in canary? risk is prefault causing regressive cold-start but should help steady state.
Tim: quick repro command to iterate load & log allocation decisions:
```
RUNTIME_DEBUG=kv_alloc_verbose KVPAGER_MODE=hybrid ./loadtest --model paged-attn --seq 2048 --concurrency 80 --duration 5m
```
This emits `alloc_hint`, `allocation_result`, `pager_event` lines.

Maria: also noticed kernel_selector ties to alloc path: when slab_fallback_count > threshold we swap kernel to fused_attn to avoid memory blow; that's expensive for mid-length sequences. we should decouple kernel fallback from transient alloc failures (throttle/decay) so we don't flip kernel on short bursts.

Jen: actionable shortlist:
- revert kernel-selector gating (Alex)
- enable pre-reserve small slab arenas on canary (Raj + Tim)
- add metric slab_fallback_count -> telemetry + alert if > 100/min (Maria)
- run 12h canary sweep and compare p95/p99 (Jen)

Alex: I'll open the revert PR now and flag it for quick deploy. will also create the issue for allocator followups and link bench runs. :thumbsup:
Tim: I'll prototype pre-reserve patch and push a canary build to the canary queue tomorrow morning.
Raj: I'll draft the compaction GC RFC after the prototype.

Maria: logging note — include `kernel_choice_reason` in kernel_dispatch logs (enum: policy|oom|fallback) so we can pinpoint why we switched at runtime.

perf-bot: added comparison svg to CI run results (canary vs baseline) — p95 gap highlighted.

Alex: thanks all. keep updates in this thread. next sync if canary still regressing after revert + pre-reserve. :memo:
